messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager — production gateway is reporting elevated 5xx + upstream timeouts on inference route /v1/generate. Alert threshold crossed at 11:03:42 UTC. Autoscaled pool reports queue depth spike in the batching scheduler. thread_ts=1799994444

Oncall SRE: I’m on it. looking at scheduler metrics now — sending short update in 2m.

Alex G.: Seeing head-of-line build on gw-prod-gpu-3, batch queue length ~1.4k and p95 latency spikes to 12s. Many requests stuck waiting for batches.

Maya S.: Confirmed. Also seeing a surge of ~35% long-context requests (seq_len>2048) which triggers slower kernels. Could be the culprit for batch packing delays.

Ryan T.: Any customer-facing impact so far? Customer Ops, can you surface any high-priority accounts reporting errors?

Customer Ops: A few enterprise customers reported timeouts for interactive chat flows, highest-impact: acme-inc and finlytics. They see 504 from our gateway. They're asking for ETA.

Nadia (DevEx): Quick mitigation options listed: 1) Reduce max batch size to force faster flush, 2) Short-circuit long-context requests to a slower preemptible pool (falls back), 3) Temporarily disable batching for the hotspot route. Which should we try first?

Laura (Eng Runtime): Recommended order: reduce batch window (max_wait_ms -> 20ms), reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 16, and enable per-request bypass for seq_len>1024. Doing all three in concert is safest.

Oncall SRE: Applying config change to gateway -> set route-batching.window_ms=20 and scheduler.max_batch_size=16. Pushing canary to region-us-east-1 now.

LogBot: deploy-bot: canary config applied to gw-prod-us-east-1 at 11:09:03 UTC (config-id: cfg-2026-06-batch-mitigate).

Alex G.: Canary looks good, p95 down from 12s -> 1.8s on the canary hosts. But total queue length still high on older instances.

Maya S.: I’m starting an emergency scale-up for the dedicated GPU pool: +20% nodes, add 4 instances with larger memory so KV cache pressure reduces. ETA ~5m.

Oncall SRE: Rolling scale-up started. Also enabling routing fallback: traffic for model:llama-70b-opt -> model:llama-70b-opt-quant-fallback for non-critical requests to reduce load.

Ryan T.: Will fallback variant affect quality? Customer Ops, please flag high-SLA customers so we can keep them pinned to primary.

Customer Ops: Pinned acme-inc and finlytics to primary via override. Notifying them that we’re applying mitigations now.

Laura (Eng Runtime): Added a hotfix to scheduler eviction policy — evict oldest partial batch after 1500ms to prevent head-of-line stalls. Hotfix applied to canary.

LogBot: alert: scheduler-queue-eviction applied on canary hosts at 11:14:07 UTC.

Alex G.: After combined changes (batch window, smaller max batch, eviction, scale-up), error rate falling. 5xx rate down from 4.7% to 0.8% over last 2m. Gateway timeouts trending down.

Maya S.: Noted one noisy pattern: a small subset of requests repeatedly re-queuing due to malformed context (embedding length mismatch) — producing retry storms. I’m adding a filter to reject + log these at the ingress to avoid requeues.

Nadia (DevEx): For customers in dev mode, added a temporary per-customer throttle to keep platform stable.

Oncall SRE: Will keep canary for 10m, then roll to remaining hosts if stable. Keeping paging awake for follow-ups.

Alex G.: Rolling to full region at 11:25 UTC — pushing now.

LogBot: roll-batch-config: started rolling to gw-prod-us-east-1 (remaining hosts: 42) at 11:25:30 UTC.

Customer Ops: acme-inc confirmed recovery on their side at 11:27 UTC. They still want a post-incident note.

Ryan T.: Postmortem action items we should capture: 1) Add autoscaling triggers based on queue depth, 2) Add a hard-path for long-context routing to dedicated lane, 3) Improve ingress validation to avoid requeue-causing malformed requests, 4) Run load tests that include spike of long-context traffic.

Maya S.: I’ll own (2) and (3). ETA for changes: next week for routing lane, 48h for ingress validation patch.

Alex G.: I’ll own (1) and (4). Drafting a scaling rule: scale when batch_queue_length > 800 for >30s, and a faster cooldown. Also will add an e2e test harness for mixed-short-and-long inputs.

Nadia (DevEx): I’ll prepare customer-facing summary and templates for Customer Ops.

Oncall SRE: Handoff to next oncall in 30m — if anything regresses ping @Oncall+SRE. For now, marking incident as mitigated. Keeping channel open for postmortem notes.

Incident Bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident started 11:03:42 UTC, mitigated as of 11:28:15 UTC.

Alex G.: Adding a short timeline to the thread before we close.

Maya S.: Thanks team.
